cues.en: One of the better-known issues with recommender systems is what is known as the cold start problem.
cues.zh: 推薦系統較知名的問題之一，就是所謂的冷啟動問題。

cues.en: If a brand-new user arrives at your site, what do you recommend to them when you know nothing about them yet?
cues.zh: 全新的使用者來到網站，你還對他一無所知時，該推薦什麼？

cues.en: And new users aren't the only problem, what about new items in your catalog?
cues.zh: 問題不只有新使用者，商品目錄裡的新項目呢？

cues.en: How do they get recommended when there is no data on them yet to pair them with other items?
cues.zh: 還沒有任何資料能把它與其他項目配對時，要如何推薦它？

cues.en: When faced with a new user, your options are limited.
cues.zh: 面對新使用者，你的選擇很有限。

cues.en: The one saving grace is that a new user isn't new for long assuming they stay at your site at all, you'll soon have some information to work with that indicates their interests.
cues.zh: 唯一值得慶幸的是，只要他留在網站上，就不會一直是新使用者；你很快就會有一些能顯示他興趣的資訊可用。

cues.en: As soon as this new user looks at a new item, you'll have at least some implicit information about this user's interests, even if it's just that this user looked at this product.
cues.zh: 只要這位新使用者看了一個新項目，就至少有一點關於他興趣的隱含資訊，即使只是知道他看過這項產品。

cues.en: If you're lucky, they landed on your site on an actual product page, and you can just recommend other items similar to the item they are looking at.
cues.zh: 如果幸運，他一開始就來到某個產品頁面，你就能推薦與他正在看的項目相似的其他項目。

cues.en: As it turns out, the thing a person is looking at right now is actually the strongest indication of what they are interested in right now.
cues.zh: 事實上，一個人此刻正在看的東西，正是他此刻興趣最強烈的訊號。

cues.en: That's why people who bought this also bought is such a successful feature on Amazon and it works even for people who aren't logged in, or are brand-new to Amazon.
cues.zh: 這就是為什麼 Amazon 的「買過這個的人也買過」如此成功，而且即使沒登入，或剛開始使用 Amazon，也一樣有效。

cues.en: All they need to know is what you're looking at right now, and recommending products similar to that is a really safe bet.
cues.zh: 系統只需要知道你現在在看什麼，推薦類似的產品，就是相當穩妥的做法。

cues.en: But, if a new user just lands on your home page, you really don't have much to work with.
cues.zh: 但如果新使用者只是來到首頁，你真的沒有太多資訊可用。

cues.en: A fair question to ask, however, is whether this really is a new user or not.
cues.zh: 不過，有個合理問題：這真的是新使用者嗎？

cues.en: Perhaps they are actually an existing customer who just hasn't logged in yet.
cues.zh: 他也許其實是既有顧客，只是還沒登入。

cues.en: Sometimes you can use browser cookies to help identify users even when they are logged out, and tie the user session to a user account for use in making recommendations.
cues.zh: 有時即使使用者登出，也能透過瀏覽器 cookie 協助辨識，將工作階段連結到使用者帳號，以產生推薦。

cues.en: You have to be really careful about this, however.
cues.zh: 不過，這件事必須非常小心。

cues.en: The world is enacting stricter and stricter laws on how websites use cookies, and if you get a users' identity wrong, you can end up in a real mess if you recommend items to someone based on somebody else's interests.
cues.zh: 世界各地對網站使用 cookie 制定越來越嚴格的法律。而且如果認錯使用者，根據別人的興趣推薦給他，可能惹出大麻煩。

cues.en: That would be a real violation of user privacy.
cues.zh: 那會嚴重侵犯使用者隱私。

cues.en: There is one thing you know about anybody who lands on your website, and that's the IP address they are connecting from.
cues.zh: 對每個來到網站的人，你都知道一件事，就是他連線使用的 IP 位址。

cues.en: Many IP addresses can be translated into geographical locations, or at least a good guess of where the user is connecting from.
cues.zh: 許多 IP 位址能轉換成地理位置，至少能大致猜出使用者從哪裡連線。

cues.en: So you could imagine building up a database of people from this region liked these items using a similarity metric between places and items, instead of people and items.
cues.zh: 所以可以想像，建立「這個地區的人喜歡這些項目」的資料庫，改用地點與項目之間的相似度衡量，而非人與項目。

cues.en: You could then recommend items that are uniquely popular in the area you think this user is located.
cues.zh: 接著推薦在你推測使用者所在區域，特別受歡迎的項目。

cues.en: The connection between a person's location and their interests is tenuous at best, but it may be better than nothing.
cues.zh: 一個人的所在地與興趣之間，充其量只有很薄弱的關係，但可能總比沒有好。

cues.en: A safer bet is probably just to recommend top-selling items when you have nothing else to work with.
cues.zh: 如果沒有其他資訊，較穩妥的做法大概是直接推薦暢銷項目。

cues.en: Top-sellers are by definition the things a person is most likely to buy if you know nothing else about their unique interests.
cues.zh: 當你對一個人的獨特興趣一無所知時，按定義，暢銷品就是他最可能購買的東西。

cues.en: And it's a pretty easy thing to work with.
cues.zh: 而且這很容易實作。

cues.en: You're probably already computing top-sellers on your platform anyhow, all you have to do is show them to users you don't recognize.
cues.zh: 反正你的平台大概已經在計算暢銷排行，只需要顯示給無法辨識的使用者。

cues.en: You might also take this as an opportunity to promote items that your business wants to push, or that they are receiving advertising dollars for.
cues.zh: 也可以利用這個機會，推廣公司想主打，或收取廣告費的項目。

cues.en: Since you can't provide personalized recommendations, think about what the next best use of that space on your website would be.
cues.zh: 既然無法提供個人化推薦，就想想網站上的那塊空間，下一個最好的用途是什麼。

cues.en: Finally, you can straight up ask the new user what their interests are.
cues.zh: 最後，也能直接詢問新使用者的興趣。

cues.en: If you remember back to the very early days of Netflix, when you signed up they would present a bunch of popular movies to you and ask you to rate them if you had seen them, in order to get some information to work
cues.zh: 如果還記得 Netflix 非常早期的時候，註冊後會列出一批熱門電影，請你為看過的電影評分，以便取得一些，

cues.en: with on your personal interests.
cues.zh: 關於個人興趣的資訊。

cues.en: If your site really revolves around personalized recommendations, this might be a reasonable thing to do.
cues.zh: 如果網站真的以個人化推薦為核心，這可能是合理的做法。

cues.en: But, the reality is most people these days aren't going to be willing to devote that kind of time to you.
cues.zh: 但現實是，現在大多數人不願意為你投入那麼多時間。

cues.en: A lot of people will just abandon your site when you start to demand that sort of work from them, so you don't see this approach being used much these days.
cues.zh: 一旦要求他們做這些事，很多人就會離開網站，所以現在已經不太常看到這種做法。

cues.en: The other aspect of the cold start problem is how to deal with new items.
cues.zh: 冷啟動問題的另一個面向，是如何處理新項目。

cues.en: When a new item is introduced into your catalog, how will it get recommended to users when there is no data to associate it with other items or other users yet?
cues.zh: 商品目錄加入新項目時，還沒有資料能把它與其他項目或使用者連結，要如何推薦給使用者？

cues.en: Well, one option is to just not worry about it.
cues.zh: 一種選擇就是先不用管它。

cues.en: Presumably, there are other ways for users to discover new items on your website than recommendations.
cues.zh: 使用者在網站上發現新項目的方式，應該不只有推薦。

cues.en: They will show up in search results, they might appear in promotions, and the maker of the item is probably advertising it in hopes that people will search for it and buy it on your site.
cues.zh: 新項目會出現在搜尋結果，可能出現在促銷活動，製造商大概也會打廣告，希望人們到你的網站搜尋並購買。

cues.en: As soon as people start indicating their interest in this new item through these other items, then your recommender system will start to pick up on it.
cues.zh: 只要人們開始透過這些其他途徑，表現出對新項目的興趣，推薦系統就會開始捕捉到它。

cues.en: In practice I've found this to be a perfectly reasonable approach.
cues.zh: 實務上，我覺得這是完全合理的做法。

cues.en: But, some researchers do consider this a real problem and have proposed other solutions.
cues.zh: 但有些研究人員確實把它視為問題，並提出其他解法。

cues.en: If you remember way back to the beginning of this course, we talked about content-based recommenders.
cues.zh: 如果還記得課程最前面，我們談過內容式推薦。

cues.en: Even if you have no activity data on this new item, you have data on its attributes, its title, its description, its category, and probably other stuff as well.
cues.zh: 即使沒有這個新項目的活動資料，你仍有屬性資料，例如標題、說明、類別，可能還有其他資訊。

cues.en: You can use that to recommend it alongside items that have similar attributes.
cues.zh: 可以利用這些資料，將它和屬性相似的項目一起推薦。

cues.en: Making recommendations based on content attributes alone is never a good idea, but if you augment your behavior-based recommendations with content-based ones, that solves the item cold start problem right there.
cues.zh: 只根據內容屬性做推薦，向來不是好主意；但如果用內容式推薦補充行為式推薦，就能解決項目的冷啟動問題。

cues.en: Let's say you're generating top-10 recommendations for a user based on ratings data, but you can only come up with eight good recommendations.
cues.zh: 假設根據評分資料，為使用者產生前十名推薦，卻只能找到八個好的推薦。

cues.en: Maybe those last two slots can be filled by content-based recommendations, which might surface new items.
cues.zh: 也許最後兩個位置能放內容式推薦，這就可能讓新項目曝光。

cues.en: Taking that idea even further is merging content attributes with latent features learned from ratings behavior.
cues.zh: 進一步延伸這個想法，就是把內容屬性與從評分行為學到的潛在特徵合併。

cues.en: If you learn latent features through matrix factorization or deep learning, perhaps you can associate those latent features with content attributes, and use the behavior patterns you learned
cues.zh: 如果透過矩陣分解或深度學習學習潛在特徵，也許能把這些潛在特徵連結到內容屬性，並用從既有項目學到的行為模式，

cues.en: from existing items to inform relationships with new items.
cues.zh: 協助推論與新項目的關係。

cues.en: It's a pretty complicated idea, but if you want to learn more, look up a paper called LearnAROMA that details this approach.
cues.zh: 這個想法相當複雜。如果想深入了解，可以搜尋一篇叫做 LearnAROMA 的論文，裡面詳細介紹這個方法。

cues.en: It's definitely bleeding-edge territory, but it's a neat idea.
cues.zh: 這絕對是非常前沿的領域，但想法很有意思。

cues.en: Finally, there's the idea of random exploration.
cues.zh: 最後還有隨機探索這個想法。

cues.en: We talked about using extra slots in your top-N recommendations to surface content-based recommendations, but those content-based recommendations could be from new or old items.
cues.zh: 我們談過，利用 Top-N 推薦中的額外位置呈現內容式推薦，但這些內容式推薦可能是新項目，也可能是舊項目。

cues.en: If you really want to tackle this problem directly, you could dedicate those extra slots to just randomly showing new items to users, in an attempt to gather more data on them and surface them to users more quickly.
cues.zh: 如果想直接解決這個問題，可以把額外位置專門用來隨機向使用者展示新項目，嘗試蒐集更多資料，也讓它們更快曝光。

cues.en: I'm not really sold on this approach, because a brand new item isn't likely to be something a user recognizes, so I don't think they're likely to click on them.
cues.zh: 我對這種方法並不完全信服，因為全新的項目不太可能是使用者認得的，所以我不覺得他們很可能會點擊。

cues.en: But, if you truly have nothing better to show to a user in that real estate on your website, it might be a reasonable thing to do.
cues.zh: 但如果網站上那塊空間，真的沒有更好的內容能顯示給使用者，那這可能是合理的做法。

cues.en: It's pretty easy, so let's go ahead and give it a try.
cues.zh: 它很容易實作，就來試試看。
